standard.title: Media arts across cultures and times
standard.description: explore where, why and how media arts is created and/or distributed across cultures, times, places and/or other contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can explain why media arts works matter to communities and describe the role of media artists. They have explored media arts from their own and First Nations Australian communities. They have not yet explored media arts across historical periods or analysed representations and stereotypes across different social contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore where, why and how media arts is created and/or distributed across cultures, times, places and/or other contexts — comparing works made for different purposes and identifying how context shapes representation.

nodes.label: Context shapes representation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify how social, cultural or historical context shapes the representations and meanings in a media arts work.
nodes.minimum_width: Examine one media arts work from a context different from their own (different time, culture or social context) and identify at least one way the context shapes the characters, stories or values in the work.
nodes.typical_width: Examine media arts works from different social, cultural and historical contexts; identify and describe representations, stereotypes and storytelling conventions; compare how the same topic (e.g. heroes, family) is represented differently across contexts; use appropriate media arts language.
wider: Investigate how traditional First Nations Australian stories are being retold using media technologies (animation, stop motion, green screen) — examining how media arts concepts (framing, sound, editing) serve cultural storytelling purposes different from mainstream media conventions

Compare how the same type of story (e.g. a superhero narrative) is told across different cultural or historical contexts — identifying what values, representations and conventions differ, and what this reveals about the contexts
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding how context shapes representation is the conceptual foundation for media literacy at Y3-4 — without it, students read media works as neutral rather than constructed, which blocks more sophisticated analysis.

response_modes.reason: Students need explicit scaffolding to move from 'this is what the work shows' to 'the context shaped this representation' — use structured comparison questions: 'Why would a filmmaker from this time/place represent it this way?'

success_criteria: Student can identify at least one way a media arts work's context shapes its representations or values
Student can use at least one piece of media arts language (e.g. 'representation', 'convention', 'stereotype') to describe what they found

nodes.label: Purpose, distribution and comparison
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can compare media arts works made for different purposes and identify features that serve those purposes — including how the same story might be told differently across media types.
nodes.minimum_width: Compare two media arts works made for different purposes (e.g. a news story and an advertisement) and identify at least two features that differ and explain why.
nodes.typical_width: Compare media arts works made for different purposes (entertainment, persuasion, information, cultural preservation) using appropriate language; investigate how conventions vary across media types; use language of media arts to discuss meaning; investigate storyboarding as a planning tool across different media forms.
wider: Compare how the same event or topic is represented across different media types (news report, advertisement, social media post, animated retelling) — identifying how purpose and platform shape representation and what a viewer might understand differently from each

Investigate how media arts works are distributed for different purposes and contexts (school intranet, community event, broadcasting, cultural festivals) — discussing how distribution context affects who the audience is and what the work communicates

response_modes.reason: Vary the comparison contexts — news, advertising, cultural storytelling, entertainment — to ensure students develop a broad understanding of how purpose shapes form, not just a narrow comparison of two similar works.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of media types and purposes available for comparison at Y3-4 (news, advertising, cultural storytelling, animation, stop motion) is genuinely rich — students who compare across multiple types develop much stronger critical media literacy.
success_criteria: Student can compare two media arts works made for different purposes
Student can identify at least two features that differ between them and explain why those differences serve the different purposes
